Seattle Sounders FC vs Real Salt Lake

Sunday, October 25, 2015

Kickoff: 4PM

Royal Brougham Park (CenturyLink Field)

Seattle Washington

By Glenn White

It all comes down to this.

Decades from now, scorelines become footnotes. The players on the bench unsubstituted misremembered. Those in the Brougham End come and go. The millions of little things that make up a match day. Most of them will be lost to photos, comments on the internet, a corner of a videoclip.

But there are moments that last forever. Fredy's first. Keller's quadruple save against San Jose in his last match. Steve Zakuani taking the pitch again. Dempsey unzipping a hoodie. Raising an incredible fourth US Open Cup in six years in Philadelphia. Raising the long-elusive Supporters Shield over the Brougham End.

This season: Dempsey tearing up a ref's notebook and walking away. Any one of a number of Oba's goals. Finally reacquiring the long-lost Cascadia Cup from our northern rivals in their own den. Not much more.

This match is a play-in match. Win and we're in. Lose, and we're subject to relying on the results of three other matches. You could break this down into scenarios and what-ifs...but it doesn't really matter: Win and we're in. An opportunity ripe for a moment.

Getting knocked out of US Open Cup play by Portland and so many cards and injuries, if it weren't the US Open Cup, and it wasn't Portland, would have been hysterical. It was certainly historical. Finished with seven players. Doesn't matter. Win and we're in.

A July and August that Chivas could have put together. Without a squad. Doesn't matter. Win and we're in.

So many hamstring injuries, it makes one seriously wonder what's in the water in Seattle. Doesn't matter. Win and we're in.

Signing arguably the best centerback in CONCACAF only to see him fall to a knee injury a few weeks later. Doesn't matter. Win and we're in.

You see where this is going.

One moment turns this season into the 2015 MLS Playoffs. One memorable moment. One curving left footed shot. One outstretched desperate palm for a goalline clearance. One tackle, one shot, one save. One goal.

There will always be what-ifs and if-onlys. Doesn't matter.

One moment.

MLS Cup is a long way away. First Kick 2015 is a long way behind us. The only thing that matters now is Sunday. Is winning one match.

Get in.
